newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan domestic car sales up in Jan before tax hike.
newsitem.headline: Japan domestic car sales up in Jan before tax hike.

text.p: Japan's domestic car sales got off to a quick start in 1997, posting double-digit gains in January, helped by demand from consumers rushing to buy cars ahead of a sales tax increase in April.

Vehicle sales, excluding 660cc minivehicles, rose 14.9 percent in January from a year earlier to 336,642 units, the fifth successive month they rose on a year-on-year basis, the Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said on Monday.

The January sales were also a record high for the month, surpassing the previous record of 325,468 in January 1990, partly due to greater demand ahead of an increase in Japan's consumption tax, which will be raised to five percent from three percent from April 1.
"The results of the January sales were as expected," said Kankaku Research senior analyst Nobuaki Yanachi.
All Japanese makers marked year-on-year gains in January, except Isuzu which saw a decline in sales of its heavy sports-utility vehicles as consumers switched to lighter models.
The carmakers expect their domestic sales to continue to climb ahead of the consumption tax hike.

Honda's January sales totalled 38,373, a record high for a January and up 54.5 percent from the previous record 24,843 in January last year, as sales of its recreation vehicles boomed, a Honda spokesman said.

Demand for recreation vehicles such as Honda's CR-V and Toyota's RAV4 have risen at the expense of heavier recreation vehicles, such as the Isuzu Big Horn and Mitsubishi Motors', Pajero since the Toyota RAV4 was introduced in May 1994, industry sources said.
Isuzu plans to introduce a new recreational vehicle in Japan this spring.
Ailing carmaker Mazda also marked a steep 22.7 percent gain in January to 23,775 vehicles, helped by demand for its compact recreational Demio model.
Sales are likely to continue posting year-on-year gains ahead of April's consumption tax hike, a Mazda spokesman said.
In December, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association forecast that Japan's domestic vehicle sales in 1997 would total 7.02 million units, slightly lower than the 7.08 million sold in 1996.

Overall domestic sales, including 660cc minivehicles, are likely to reach 7.1 million or 7.2 million units in 1997 because of the increased demand ahead of the tax hike and replacement demand from consumers with older models, Yanachi said.
